    "governance": [
      {
        "slug": "principle-extraction",
        "name": "Principle Extraction",
        "description": "A move that lifts a heuristic out of specific experience and elevates it to a principle — a named rule, an aphorism, an invariant the writer intends others to adopt. The failure mode is over-generalization: treating a pattern that held in one or two cases as universal. Principles are load-bearing once canonized; pressure here is about sample size, counter-examples, and scope."
      },
      {
        "slug": "observation",
        "name": "Observation",
        "description": "A report of something seen or noticed, offered without strong claim or directive. Observations are the lightest-pressure claim type. They deserve sample-representativeness and context questions, not adversarial scrutiny. This is the fallback type — inputs that match no other type route here."
      },
      {
        "slug": "strong-claim",
        "name": "Strong Claim",
        "description": "A definitive statement offered without qualification. Strong claims foreclose doubt and deserve the most pressure, because their cost of being wrong is proportional to the confidence they project."
      },
      {
        "slug": "comparative-positioning",
        "name": "Comparative Positioning",
        "description": "A claim that locates this work against other work — existing approaches, adjacent projects, viral repositories, published papers, competing frameworks. Comparative positioning lives or dies on whether the comparison target is characterized honestly and freshly. The failure mode is strawmanning, selective citation, or comparing against a stale snapshot of something that has since evolved."
      },
      {
        "slug": "proposal",
        "name": "Proposal",
        "description": "A future-oriented plan or recommendation. Proposals carry their weight in the options they close. Pressure here is about alternatives considered, reversibility, and what would need to be true for the proposal to fail."
      }
    ],
    "governance_source": "knowledge_base",
    "governance_uris": [
      "klappy://odd/challenge/base-prerequisites",
      "klappy://odd/challenge-types",
      "klappy://odd/challenge/normative-vocabulary",
      "klappy://odd/challenge/stakes-calibration"
    ],
    "tensions": [],
    "missing_prerequisites": [
      "No evidence cited — a claim without grounding in something observed, read, or experienced is just a belief",
      "Confidence level not signaled — is this a guess, a working belief, or an established fact?",
      "Principle not anchored to multiple cases — one observation is a pattern; one pattern is a principle only with more cases",
      "No counter-examples considered — a principle without acknowledged limits is a bias in formalwear",
      "Strong claim lacks explicit evidence — strength of claim should match strength of evidence",
      "No disconfirmer acknowledged — what would change this claim?",
      "Comparison target not specifically named — 'existing approaches' is not a comparison",
      "No shared ground acknowledged — honest comparison names similarities before differences",
      "No alternatives mentioned — single-option proposals lack rigor",
      "Reversibility not addressed — irreversible proposals deserve proportional scrutiny",
      "No success criteria named — how will you know if this worked?"
    ],
    "challenges": [
      "How many distinct cases does this principle rest on? One, two, many?",
      "What's a counter-example you considered and rejected?",
      "What's the scope? Does this hold for a specific domain, or are you making a universal claim?",
      "Under what conditions would you retract this principle?",
      "Is this observation based on a representative sample?",
      "What context might change this observation?",
      "Is this one data point, or a pattern?",
      "What evidence would disprove this?",
      "Under what conditions does this NOT hold?",
      "Who or what would disagree with this, and why?",
      "What is the strongest version of the opposing view?",
      "Is the comparison target fairly represented or characterized in its weakest form?",
      "When was the comparison target last examined? Has it changed since?",
      "Have you engaged the strongest version of the compared work, or the most convenient?",
      "What is the compared work trying to solve that yours isn't, and vice versa?",
      "What's the cost of being wrong here?",
      "What alternatives were considered and rejected, and why?",
      "What would need to be true for this to fail?",
      "Is this reversible? If not, what's the point of no return?"
    ],
    "suggested_reframings": [
      "Reframe as scoped rule: \"In the context of C, the pattern I've seen is X; outside C, I don't know\"",
      "Reframe with sample: \"Across cases A, B, and D, I observe X; I treat this as a principle within that class\"",
      "Reframe as working heuristic: \"My current working rule is X; I'd revise it if I encountered W\"",
      "Reframe as hypothesis under test: \"I'm treating X as a principle; the cases that would challenge it are A, B, C, and I'll watch for them\"",
      "Reframe with context: \"In situation X, I observed Y; outside X, I have not checked\"",
      "Distinguish instance from pattern: \"This happened once\" vs \"This happens consistently under condition C\"",
      "Reframe as hypothesis: \"We believe X because Y, and would reconsider if Z\"",
      "Reframe with scope: \"In contexts A and B, X holds; outside those, we have not tested\"",
      "Reframe as falsifiable: \"If we observed W, we would retract this claim\"",
      "Reframe with fairness: \"X and my approach share A and B; they diverge on C, where X does Y and I do Z\"",
      "Reframe with recency: \"As of [date/version], X does Y; I'm aware this may have changed\"",
      "Reframe with humility: \"I may be mischaracterizing X; the claim holds against my reading of their docs as of [date]\"",
      "Reframe to acknowledge strongest version: \"The strongest defense of X is A; my claim is that even granting A, Z still holds\"",
      "Add optionality: \"We're choosing X over Y because Z, reversible until W\"",
      "Reframe with stakes: \"This is a one-way door; we are committing because A, B, C\"",
      "Reframe as experiment: \"We'll try X for duration D; success looks like M; we'll abandon if N\"",
      "Address canon tensions directly before proceeding"
    ],
